LESSON: WRITING 8.5.1 ASSESSMENT OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.5: Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what the others have done. 1. How does a text with errors make you feel?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify errors in an essay written by self or peers
2. appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 8.5.1 ASSESSMENT OF WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 8.5.1 ASSESSMENT OF WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify errors in an essay written by self or peers

What this means
In this part you learn to identify errors in an essay written by self or peers. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify errors in an essay written by self or peers.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify errors in an essay written by self or peers. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify errors in an essay written by self or peers)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing to a partner. (skill: appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify errors in an essay written by self or peers.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what the others have done. 1. How does a text with errors make you feel?
2. What are some of the common mistakes we make in our writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify errors in an essay written by self or peers.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
